attacks.claim: The mandated public announcement says texts are for every cardholder, but the artifact says juvenile cards never see the SMS option. Under-13 and juvenile patrons will be told to opt in and find nothing, and the poster and newsletter copy is irreversible once published.
attacks.evidence: Announcement text says exactly: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." Contradicted by: "juvenile cards do not show it"

attacks.claim: The $900 cap applies only to the SMS provider. When it trips, every opted-in patron falls back to automated phone calls, which have no stated budget, forecast, or cap. The fallback is most likely to fire during a surge, so spend moves to an uncapped channel.
attacks.evidence: "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)"; forecast covers only "38,000 texts/month"

attacks.claim: The launch flips the flag for all ~210k cardholders at once, and all overnight queued texts flush at 08:00. No throughput, rate-limit, or volume test appears in QA, so a 08:00 burst could exceed 10DLC or provider throughput and delay or fail hold alerts for the whole system.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00"; "flags on for all cardholders"; QA rows cover only "500 generated holds" for content and a 64-staff pilot; no load row

attacks.claim: Five wrong codes lock a locker cell, but the artifact gives no unlock or reset path, no lockout duration, and no explanation of how a cell is chosen. A person holding any valid card could repeatedly enter wrong codes and lock cells across a bank, blocking 24/7 pickup until staff intervene under a 4-hour vendor SLA.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff"; ABSENT: unlock/reset procedure, lockout duration, and cell-selection logic. Monitoring alerts only on "any locker bank offline > 10 min"

attacks.claim: STOP opt-out depends on the webhook clearing the opt-in flag, but only webhook signature failures alert. A dropped or failed STOP webhook goes unnoticed and leaves local state out of sync with the provider, which can inflate delivery-failure alerts.
attacks.evidence: "STOP ... is honored by the provider and our signed webhook, which clears the opt-in flag"; alerts: "webhook signature failures > 0" (no delivery-gap alert)

attacks.claim: Locker accessibility features (ADA reach, audio guidance, high contrast, text size) were acceptance-tested only by vendor and branch staff. None of the QA rows test them with assistive technology or a user who relies on them.
attacks.evidence: "Touchscreen and card reader mounted within ADA reach range ... audio guidance through a headphone jack"; QA covers screen readers only for "Opt-in form"; ABSENT: locker accessibility QA row

attacks.claim: Phone number and IP address are retained for as long as a patron stays opted in, and no retention period for active consent records is stated. The 30-day purge covers only the notification log.
attacks.evidence: "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record"; ABSENT: retention period while opted in

attacks.claim: Guardians can opt in on the linked account, but the artifact does not say what a guardian's phone receives for a juvenile's holds. If it includes a minor's hold or pickup details, disclosure to a guardian may conflict with state minors' library-record rules.
attacks.evidence: "guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account"; ABSENT: content and scope of guardian texts

attacks.claim: Batched texts use a single template that names one locker, but holds can be at different pickup points. A patron with a locker hold and a desk hold could receive a message pointing to the wrong location.
attacks.evidence: "extra holds are batched into one message"; sample: "2 holds ready at Oak St locker"

attacks.claim: Texts queued to 08:00 may carry codes for holds already collected or cancelled. The artifact does not say whether queued messages are re-validated, and the time zone for code expiry is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00"; "Codes are single-use, expire at the pickup deadline"

attacks.claim: Rolling back locker_pickup remaps holds and extends deadlines, but it does not say whether codes already sent by SMS stay valid, or how patrons are notified if sms_holds is also off.
attacks.evidence: "hold deadlines extend 3 days and patrons are notified of the new location"; ABSENT: code validity after remap and notification channel when SMS is off

attacks.claim: Hold notifications depend on one SMS provider with no secondary, and the fallback phone-call vendor is not named. Switching providers would require re-registering the 10DLC campaign and rebuilding opt-in state.
attacks.evidence: "the SMS provider is an existing vendor under a signed DPA"; "10DLC brand and campaign are registered"

attacks.claim: The DPA is asserted to cover SMS message content, which includes locker codes and branch linked to a patron, but no clause or scope is cited. The DPA predates this product.
attacks.evidence: "The SMS provider is covered by our existing DPA (signed 2025-03)"; ABSENT: DPA clause covering SMS content

attacks.claim: Only English message copy is shown. The Spanish templates, which are part of the launch, are not reviewed in the artifact.
attacks.evidence: "English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference"; sample message is English only
